render_lambertian — 3D photometric op

• Data kinds: normalmap → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.render_lambertian(normals, albedo, light, ambient=0.0) (to call the implementation directly, import photometric; photometric.render_lambertian(normals, albedo, light, ambient=0.0); from the registry, ops3d.get("render_lambertian"))

Usage

Normals + albedo + light direction → a Lambertian image (inspection-sample generation / GT verification / the forward model of inverse rendering). → HxW.

I = albedo * (max(n·L, 0) + ambient). light is a (3,) light-direction vector, normalised internally to unit length (its length has no effect as intensity). Pixels with n·L < 0 are clipped to 0 (attached shadow). ambient is a constant added uniformly regardless of the normal, and the albedo multiplies it (default 0). normals are (H,W,3) normals (assumed unit length, not normalised), albedo is (H,W) or a broadcastable array / scalar. Returns float32 (H,W). The upper bound is albedo * (1 + ambient); there is no clipping to [0,1]. There is no input validation. It is exactly the forward model of photometric_stereo (the light-normalisation convention corresponds to normalize=True), so it can be used for round-trip verification: re-synthesise from the recovered normals and albedo and compare with the original images. Specular reflection, interreflection and cast shadows are not included.
